description: Strava Metro aggregates, de-identifies and contextualises the activities that Strava users record while cycling, walking and running, and provides them to public agencies as active transportation data. Departments of transportation, planning organisations, trail organisations and cities use it to see where people ride and walk, to plan new bicycle and pedestrian infrastructure, to place counters and bike share stations and to measure behaviour change after a project; Strava reports about 4,500 partners. Coverage is global, wherever Strava users record activities, since the service began in 2014. Access: free of charge to agencies and researchers through a Metro partnership application; data are delivered through the Metro platform, and some regional extracts are shared by research data services. Privacy: the data are aggregated and de-identified consistent with the GDPR and the CCPA, and exclude private activities, hidden start and end portions and members who opted out. Caveats: Strava users are a self-selected sample, so counts need adjustment with bike counter data, and the public Global Heatmap is normalised and not suitable for volume comparison. It supports active mobility demand estimation, route choice and network flow studies, and complements the Propensity to Cycle Tool and BikeMaps.org catalogued here.
